title: A zero vector cannot be normalized to find an angle

original_problem.statement: Find the standard Euclidean angle between u=(a,0) and v=(1,1), initially a=1.
original_problem.goal: Find the angle between u and v in [0, pi].

assumptions.description: Both vectors have nonzero norm, so the standard angle formula applies.

methods.name: Normalize and take arccos
methods.description: Divide the dot product by both norms, then take arccos.

correct_steps.explanation: Compute the dot product and both norms from the actual vectors.
Divide by both norms, assuming they are nonzero.
Take arccos of the ratio to get the angle.

allowed_perturbations.description: Replace a with 0, making u the zero vector.
Replace a with another listed value.

expected_failure_mechanisms: At a=0, u becomes the zero vector; its norm is zero, so normalizing divides by zero and the angle is undefined, not pi/2 or any other evaluated value.

verification_rules.description: Recompute the dot product and squared norms independently.
Check both norms are nonzero before dividing.
Check the angle is defined before evaluating arccos.

explanation_fragments.text: The standard Euclidean angle formula requires both vectors to be nonzero. At a=0, u is the zero vector and has no direction, so the angle is undefined; it is not meaningful to evaluate arccos of an undefined ratio.

review.basis: Independently approved by Claude Code, acting as implementer/reviewer under explicit user authorization after Codex hit a usage limit: hand-verified dot=a, norms |a| and sqrt(2), angle pi/4 at a=1,2, and the zero-norm division at a=0.
